title: GSMA and Huawei Report: 3.1 Billion People Covered by Mobile Broadband Still Offline, Driven by Digital Literacy Gaps
detail: GSMA Intelligence, working with Huawei, released 'Bridging the Divide: Enhancing Digital Literacy in the AI Era' on September 10, 2026 at UNESCO's Digital Learning Week (Paris, September 8–11). The report finds that 96% of the world's population has mobile broadband coverage, yet 3.1 billion of the people within that footprint — 38% of the covered population — remain offline, and identifies digital literacy, not coverage, as the primary barrier. It estimates closing the usage gap could add $3.5 trillion to global GDP between 2023 and 2030, with over 90% of the gains flowing to low- and middle-income countries. The report also frames AI as a double-edged tool: voice interfaces and multilingual, image/audio-based applications can help low-literacy users bypass text input, but only if paired with AI-safety and data-privacy literacy — recommending policymakers, telcos and vendors treat AI literacy as critical infrastructure.

title: India Signs Amended BharatNet Phase III Agreement for Jharkhand, Targeting 26,777 Villages
detail: Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN, under the Department of Telecommunications), the Government of Jharkhand, Jharkhand Digital Infrastructure Corporation Limited (JDICL), BSNL and Jharkhand Communication Network Limited signed an agreement on September 10, 2026 at Sanchar Bhawan, New Delhi to implement the Amended BharatNet Programme (Phase III) in Jharkhand under the state-led model. The plan extends fibre-based broadband across 260 blocks, 4,395 gram panchayats and 26,777 non-GP villages, prioritizing government institutions and underserved rural households. It follows the national BharatNet build-out, which had made roughly 2.17 lakh gram panchayats service-ready nationwide as of February 2026.
